lesson_title: The T-shirt That Shows How the Economy Connects
hook_text: You paid R120 for a T-shirt. Here is exactly where that money went.
clip_script: A cotton farmer grows the cotton for one T-shirt and sells it for R10. Primary sector. A factory spins, weaves, dyes and sews it, and sells the shirt to a shop for R60. It added R50. Secondary sector. The shop trucks it in, hangs it up, advertises it and sells it to you for R120. It added R60. Tertiary sector. Add up what each step added: 10 plus 50 plus 60. R120. Exactly what you paid. Your money is shared along the chain, and every link is somebody's job. Now cut a link. If a mine closes, the boot factory that supplied it loses work, and the shops, taxis and salons in town lose customers. One closure ripples through all three sectors. The economy is not three separate parts. It is one chain.
visual_style: A T-shirt travelling along a glowing chain from a cotton field to a factory to a shop, with value tags stacking up; then one link snapping and ripples spreading across a small mining town.
mood: Insightful, connected, slightly dramatic at the break.
pacing: Steady three-step build, a satisfying sum, a sharp ripple ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and map the value chain of something you own.
